title: Update release notes for runtime 1.22.0 (FP8/INT8 perf sprint)
author: Connor O'Brien
description: Summary: Finalize the runtime 1.22.0 release notes for the FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint outcomes. This PR consolidates the kernel + scheduler changes that shipped behind flags, documents the rollout/canary plan and rollback triggers, and adds explicit guardrails/limitations discovered during the sprint (shape regimes, long-context caveats, and per-region canary learnings). It also aligns wording with Perf Transparency guidance so the same notes can be used internally (release channel) without accidentally making externally-unapproved benchmark claims. Context: This release packages the work from ENG-7422/7423/7424/7425/7426/7427/7430/7431 including (a) FP8 attention kernel integration behind flags, (b) INT8 matmul dispatch + shape guardrails and fallback behavior, (c) kernel auto-selection heuristics for H100/A100 with safe fallbacks, (d) scheduler knob defaults for mixed prefill/decode workloads, and (e) perf canary gating by model/region with improved metric tagging. What’s in the notes: Release highlights, flag names + default states, expected perf impact ranges (TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s) expressed as ranges and conditioned on workload and GPU SKU, known limitations/unsupported shapes, quality sign-off requirements for enabling quantized defaults, and operational verification checklist for SRE + oncall. No functional code changes beyond docs/changelog metadata.
commits: docs(runtime): refresh 1.22.0 highlights + link to perf canary runbook

release_notes: Runtime 1.22.0 (FP8/INT8 perf sprint) — Highlights: Adds FP8 attention kernel path (H100 first) and INT8 matmul dispatch with correctness-first fallback; Introduces kernel auto-selection heuristics for H100/A100 across common shape regimes; Updates scheduler defaults for mixed prefill/decode to better realize kernel wins end-to-end; Adds perf canary gating by model/region with improved metric tagging (model/gpu/kernel_mode) for faster regression isolation. Flags (server-side): runtime.kernels.fp8_attention.enable (default: OFF globally; ON in canary cohorts only); runtime.kernels.int8_matmul.enable (default: OFF; may be enabled per-model after eval sign-off); runtime.kernels.autoselect_quantized.enable (default: ON in canary only; OFF elsewhere until rollout completes); runtime.scheduler.mixed_workload_tuning.enable (default: ON). Expected performance impact (representative; conditioned on workload distribution and batch/concurrency): H100: decode TPOT improvements typically 6–18% with FP8 attention enabled for supported shapes; prefill improvements typically 3–10% when autoselect picks FP8/INT8 kernels; end-to-end tokens/s improvements typically 5–15% when scheduler mixed-workload tuning is enabled and traffic has moderate concurrency. A100: INT8 matmul can improve prefill-heavy workloads 4–12% for supported shapes; FP8 attention is not enabled by default (limited coverage + rollout pending). Known limitations / guardrails: FP8 attention currently gated to specific shape regimes (see flags doc) and will fall back to baseline kernels outside guardrails; A subset of long-context prompts showed quality sensitivity under FP8 for one model family — enabling FP8 defaults requires eval sign-off per the Quantization Profile Policy; INT8 matmul requires alignment/shape constraints; unsupported shapes hard-fallback to baseline to preserve correctness; Perf canary will auto-rollback on sustained TTFT/TPOT regression beyond thresholds (see canary profiles) and may be noisy on small sample sizes — use per-model cohorts and minimum-sample checks; Region-specific variance can occur with driver/CUDA mismatches; benchmark claims must include methodology footnotes and GPU/driver details (internal-only unless approved). Verification checklist: Confirm flag states per cohort; Monitor TTFT/TPOT/tokens/s + error rate + GPU mem; Validate fallback rates are within expected bounds; If canary rollback triggers, capture metadata (git SHA/CUDA/driver/clocks/model hash) and file regression issue referencing perf dashboards + nsys trace if applicable.
